fixes.before: ≈ n³/3 + n² − n/3 (i.e. (n³−n)/3 for elimination + n(n+1)/2 for back substitution); O(n³)
fixes.after: n³/3 + n² − n/3 operations (counting each division as one operation): elimination (n³−n)/3 multiply-adds + n(n−1)/2 divisions; back substitution n(n−1)/2 multiply-adds + n divisions; O(n³)

fixes.before: Proved by structural induction on arithmetic expression parse trees
fixes.after: Base n = 3: a triangle has 0 = 3·0/2 diagonals. Step: inserting a vertex v between adjacent vertices u, w of an n-gon adds n − 2 diagonals from v plus the old side uw, i.e. n − 1 new diagonals, and n(n−3)/2 + (n−1) = (n+1)(n−2)/2.
fixes.reason: Stored answer ("structural induction on arithmetic expression parse trees") is unrelated to the question; replaced with the actual induction proof.
fixes.source: GATE 1998 CSE question paper (PDF), scanned page 6

fixes.before: R = {(x,y) | x and y belong to the same block in Pi_1}; R is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive
fixes.after: Digraph on a, b, c, d with a self-loop at every vertex, arcs in both directions between every pair of a, b, c (a complete symmetric cluster), and d isolated apart from its self-loop — 10 arcs in all.
fixes.reason: Stored answer only restates the definition of R; the question asks for the graph.

fixes.before: Left/right cancellation holds under group completion
fixes.after: By associativity a*(a*a) = (a*a)*a, so a and a*a commute; the hypothesis (distinct elements never commute) forces a*a = a.
fixes.reason: Stored answer ("cancellation under group completion") is unrelated to the question.
fixes.source: GATE 1998 CSE question paper (PDF), scanned page 7

fixes.before: Associativity preserves unique identity if idempotent elements exist
fixes.after: Let x = a*b*a. Using (a): a*x = a*a*b*a = a*b*a and x*a = a*b*a*a = a*b*a, so a*x = x*a, hence x = a.
fixes.reason: Stored answer ("identity if idempotent elements exist") is unrelated to the question.
fixes.source: GATE 1998 CSE question paper (PDF), scanned page 7

fixes.before: Finite cancellative semigroup is a group
fixes.after: Let y = a*b*c, z = a*c. Using (b): y*z = a*b*(c*a*c) = a*b*c and z*y = (a*c*a)*b*c = a*b*c, so y and z commute, hence a*b*c = a*c.
fixes.reason: Stored answer ("finite cancellative semigroup is a group") is unrelated to the question.
fixes.source: GATE 1998 CSE question paper (PDF), scanned page 7

fixes.before: Instantaneous description sequence yields final accepting state q1
fixes.after: Intended PDA: in q0 it pushes one X per 1; the first 0 switches to q1; in q1 it pops one X per 1; when z0 is exposed a 0 returns to q0, and in q0 with z0 on top it may pop z0 (empty store) — so it checks blocks 1ⁿ0 1ⁿ0. As printed, only ε and 01 empty the stack.
fixes.reason: Stored answer ("final accepting state q1") is wrong: acceptance is by empty store and q1 is not special.
fixes.source: GATE 1998 CSE question paper (PDF), scanned page 7
